item.title: Lipschitz continuity - Wikipedia
item.description: In mathematical analysis, Lipschitz continuity is a regularity property of functions between metric spaces that is stronger than uniform continuity, and hence also stronger than continuity.

item.title: Rudolf Lipschitz - Wikipedia
item.description: Rudolf Otto Sigismund Lipschitz (14 May 1832 – 7 October 1903) was a German mathematician who made contributions to mathematical analysis (where he gave his name to the Lipschitz continuity condition) and differential geometry, as well as number theory, algebras with involution and classical mechanics.

item.title: Lipschitz Function -- from Wolfram MathWorld
item.description: A Lipschitz function is a function f:X->Y between metric spaces for which a constant C>=0 satisfies d_Y (f (x),f (y))<=Cd_X (x,y) for all x,y in X, where d_X and d_Y are the respective metrics (Gutev 2020).

item.title: Dr. Lipschitz - Rugrats Wiki
item.description: Dr Lipschitz is said to be inspired by a pediatrician Arline Klasky reads when raising her first child. Dr. Lipschitz is most likely a parody of real-life pediatrician Dr. Spock.

item.title: Lipschitz continuity – "Math for Non-Geeks"
item.description: Lipschitz continuity is an even stronger form of uniform continuity and is often used in the theory of differential equations.

item.title: Lipschitz continuity - HandWiki
item.description: In mathematical analysis, Lipschitz continuity, named after Germany mathematician Rudolf Lipschitz, is a strong form of uniform continuity for functions.

item.title: Lipschitz Condition -- from Wolfram MathWorld
item.description: The Lipschitz condition of order beta>0 at x=0 for a function f (x) defined near 0 states that constants B>=0 and epsilon>0 exist for which |f (h)-f (0)|<=B|h|^beta for all |h|<epsilon.

item.title: Lipschitz continuity explained
item.description: If U is a subset of the metric space M and f : U → R is a Lipschitz continuous function, there always exist Lipschitz continuous maps M → R that extend f and have the same Lipschitz constant as f (see also Kirszbraun theorem).
